validation.notes: Repaired DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions() in packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts: the bootstrap pass called settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(true) before reloading settings and resolving extensions, so any previously trusted state (or a manager created with projectTrusted: true) kept project settings and project-local .pi/extensions resolved before the trust decision, leaking project extension code into the trust bootstrap. The pass now forces setProjectTrusted(false) before settingsManager.reload(), so project settings/extensions are withheld while user/global (~/.pi agent extensions) and temporary CLI extensions stay available; reload(options.resolveProjectTrust) then applies the resolved decision and reloads, so project extensions load on top when trust is granted. Validation ran the standalone script from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0. .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads the real production modules (resource-loader.ts, settings-manager.ts, package-manager.ts) via .prale-eval/subject.mjs createGraph, faking only true boundaries (chalk/ignore/proper-lockfile defaults, config paths, extension-file loading, skills/prompts/themes) and using real fs/settings/package resolution with a temp fixture under .prale-eval/. Three assertions groups cover: (1) loadProjectTrustExtensions() from a previously trusted SettingsManager must observe isProjectTrusted() === false, expose no project settings, and resolve only the user/global and CLI extension paths while never touching the project extension path; (2) reload({resolveProjectTrust}) must show the trust callback an untrusted manager with only user/CLI extensions, then load the project extension after trust resolves true; (3) a denied trust resolution keeps project extensions out and only user/CLI loaded. Fault reproduction was confirmed: with the original setProjectTrusted(true) line temporarily restored, the same command exits 1 with AssertionError 'bootstrap pass must force untrusted project settings even when the previous state was trusted' (true !== false); with the repair in place it exits 0 printing the pass line. No dependencies, network, or package-manager installs are required; only Node builtins and the checked-in subject helper are used. The pre-existing vitest suites were not run because node_modules is absent in this workspace and dependency installation is out of scope, so the production-behavior coverage is provided by the standalone regression script above.
